noResults: No matching tasks. Try another word or choose all topics.

account.title: Create a new account
steps: On first setup, select Continue, then Create New. If you already have an account to restore, choose Import Key or Backup instead.
Reveal the recovery phrase privately. Write all 24 words in their exact order, then complete the backup check using your saved copy.
Choose a timed auto-lock setting and set and confirm a vault password. Save the password separately from the browser.
Continue through setup. Follow suggestions are optional; use Skip for now if you want to choose people later.
Select Get Started and check the account name and public key shown in the extension.
account.overview: Create a new Nostr identity when you do not already have the account you want to use. Its recovery words restore the identity; the vault password unlocks this browser.
before: Install the extension and open it from the browser toolbar.
Have a private place to record all 24 recovery words and a secure place to store them.
checks: Your account should appear in the account selector, with a public key you can copy.
If Create New opens New Sub-Account, this vault already has a main recovery phrase. The new identity will share that phrase.

subAccounts.title: Add another identity
steps: Unlock the extension, open the account selector, and choose Add Account → Create New.
Enter a name that helps you recognize the identity. The local account name does not publish a new profile name.
Keep the suggested derivation path unless you need a specific one. Open Advanced only to enter an exact path you intend to use.
Check the public-key preview, finish setup, then select the new identity in the account selector.
Record its exact derivation path and public key with your recovery records. The phrase alone does not tell another tool which path to restore.
subAccounts.overview: Create another identity for a different purpose without generating another recovery phrase. Each derived identity has its own public key, but all identities using the same phrase depend on that shared backup.
before: The vault must already contain a main recovery phrase; an imported private key alone is not enough.
Keep a secure copy of that phrase before adding identities.
checks: The account selector should show the additional identity, and selecting it should show its own public key.
Changing a path creates a different identity; it does not move posts, followers, or profile information from another account.

backup.title: Back up your account
steps: Open the account’s key or backup controls. The available options depend on whether it uses a recovery phrase, an imported private key, or a remote signer.
Save the private key or recovery backup in a secure location. Never paste private keys or recovery words into a website or a support message.
For a derived identity, save both the main recovery phrase and the exact derivation path. Include the expected public key in your recovery records.
If you create an encrypted backup, keep its password recoverable. Changing the browser’s vault password does not change an existing backup’s password.
backup.overview: A recovery backup lets you restore an account after losing this browser or device. Keep enough information to restore the exact identity, including its derivation path when it shares a recovery phrase.
before: Unlock the extension and select the account you intend to back up.
Prepare private storage for the backup and record the account’s public key so you can recognize it after recovery.
checks: Check that your saved copy is complete and readable before removing an account or clearing browser data.
When restoring later, compare the recovered public key with your saved public key. Importing a phrase does not automatically recreate every sub-account.

remove.title: Remove an account
steps: Open the account selector at the top of the extension popup.
Find the account you want to remove and select its × icon.
Read the confirmation and check the account name. For a derived account, review the path and the explanation about other accounts sharing its phrase.
Choose Remove to confirm, or Cancel to keep the account.
remove.overview: Removing an account deletes its entry from this extension. Its published profile and posts remain on Nostr, and the identity can still exist on your other devices.
before: Save a recoverable private-key or recovery backup before removing the account.
For an identity derived from a phrase, record its exact derivation path and public key too.
checks: The removed account should no longer appear in this extension’s account selector.
Removing one derived account leaves other identities from that phrase available. Restoring keys later may still require reconnecting wallets and configuring permissions.

approvals.title: Review an app’s request
steps: Open the extension’s pending request when a site asks to connect, sign, decrypt, or authenticate.
Check the requesting website and the action. Read the content or destination shown; the code button opens the raw event for closer inspection.
Choose Approve or Deny for the current request. Open an arrow menu only if you intend to remember a decision.
For grouped requests, check which requests are selected before approving the group. Revealing blurred message content does not itself approve sending it to the website.
approvals.overview: An approval request tells you what a website wants to do with the active account. A one-time decision handles that request; a remembered decision can also affect future requests.
before: Make sure the active account is the identity you want the website to use.
Check which website you are using and what action you just started there.
checks: Return to the website and check whether the action completed; review Recent activity if you need to identify the request.
An unexpected request can be denied. Review saved site or authentication permissions if similar requests are being allowed without the review you expect.

permissions.title: Change global and site rules
steps: Open Permissions → Global rules to inspect the defaults used across connected sites.
To edit the current website, open Permissions → Site rules. Gray rows are inherited defaults; colored rows are site overrides.
Use Add rule or edit an existing rule to choose Allow, Deny, or Ask for the intended action. A broader Deny can still block a request even when a narrower rule allows it.
Use Use inherited default to remove one override. To remove all overrides for this account and website, choose Reset site overrides and read the confirmation.
permissions.overview: Global rules provide shared defaults, while site rules customize ordinary actions for the active account on one website. Connection consent and backend or relay sign-ins have separate controls.
before: Select the account whose site permissions you want to change.
Open the affected website in the current browser tab before editing its site rules.
checks: Reopen the site editor and check that the intended override or inherited rule is displayed.
Resetting overrides can make a global Allow apply again. It does not remove separate connection dismissals or backend and relay authentication decisions.

authentication.title: Review saved sign-in permissions
steps: Open Permissions, then choose Backend authentication to review explicit saved backend decisions for the active account.
Revoke a saved backend decision you no longer want. Its scope includes the requesting site, exact URL, and method.
Open Relay authentication to review a relay’s allowed connected apps. Select the apps you intend to allow, or review the scope carefully before choosing all connected sites.
Review Default backend auth separately. It starts off and can allow same-origin or verified website/backend pairs automatically; read its policy link before enabling it.
authentication.overview: A website may ask to identify you to its backend or to a Nostr relay. These sign-in permissions are separate from permission to sign ordinary posts or messages.
before: Select the account whose saved sign-in decisions you want to review.
Identify the website and the backend or relay destination involved in the request.
checks: An empty backend list does not prove automatic authentication is off. Check the Default backend auth setting as well.
Revoking permission affects future approvals; it does not sign you out of an existing website session or close an already authenticated relay connection.

wallet.title: Connect a Lightning wallet
steps: Open Wallet and choose Quick Setup, NWC, or LNbits. Quick Setup creates a custodial wallet with a provider that holds the funds.
For NWC, create a dedicated connection in your wallet and copy the complete nostr+walletconnect:// secret. Allow wallet information and the operations you need.
For LNbits, enter the instance’s HTTPS URL and the wallet’s Admin API key. This is a wallet spending credential, not your administrator login password.
Connect, then check the balance and wallet activity. Use Deposit to create an invoice when you want to add sats.
wallet.overview: The extension connects to a Lightning wallet so you can check funds, receive sats, and approve payments. Choose the connection method supported by your wallet.
before: Unlock the extension and select the account that should use the wallet.
For an existing wallet, have its NWC connection secret or LNbits HTTPS URL and wallet Admin API key ready.
checks: The connected wallet should show its available balance and the features its connection permits.
If balance, invoice creation, or history is unavailable, review the connection’s permissions and expiry in your wallet. NWC and LNbits access do not by themselves determine who holds the funds.

zaps.title: Send a zap
steps: Choose the zap or Lightning button on the profile or note you want to support.
Enter the amount in sats and check which recipient the app displays.
Review any signing and payment requests in the extension. Check the amount, recipient, and fees where shown before approving.
Return to Wallet and check activity to confirm the payment outcome.
zaps.overview: A zap sends sats to someone through a compatible Nostr app. The app requests a Lightning payment from the extension’s connected wallet.
before: Connect a Lightning wallet with enough balance for the payment and any fees.
Use a Nostr app that supports paying through the extension, and check the recipient before starting.
checks: A completed payment should appear in wallet activity. The app’s visible zap result can depend on its own updates.
If the outcome is unclear, inspect wallet history before retrying. Small payments may not prompt when automatic approval is enabled and its checks pass.

appearance.title: Change the appearance
steps: Open Settings → Appearance and language.
Choose light, dark, or system appearance. Choose a theme from the available options.
Return to the dashboard and look at the text, cards, and buttons in the selected appearance.
appearance.overview: Change how the extension looks using its appearance and theme controls. These settings affect the extension interface, not the design of websites you visit.
before: Open the extension from the browser toolbar and unlock it if needed.
Decide whether you want a fixed light or dark appearance, or one that follows your system.
checks: The extension should use the selected appearance when you return to its screens.
If the result is hard to read or not what you intended, return to the same controls and choose another theme or appearance.

language.title: Change the language
steps: Open Settings → Appearance and language → Language.
Scroll or drag the language wheel until your language is centered. With the list focused, you can also use the up and down arrow keys.
Select Confirm to apply the choice. The button remains in the current interface language until you confirm.
Return to the interface and check the updated labels. Closing the picker without confirming keeps the previous language.
language.overview: Choose the language used by the extension’s controls and messages. This does not translate Nostr posts or change the website’s separate language setting.
before: Open and unlock the extension if needed.
Find Settings using the gear icon; this also helps if the current language is unfamiliar.
checks: The language row should show your saved choice when you open it again.
Some labels may remain in English. To switch back, use the gear icon and return to the same language picker.

security.title: Set a password and auto-lock
steps: Unlock the extension and open Settings → Security.
Choose a timed auto-lock interval. If you are turning timed locking on, set and confirm the password when prompted.
To replace an existing password, use Change password and complete the requested fields.
Lock the vault when finished, then unlock it using your saved password.
security.overview: A vault password protects access to the keys stored in this browser. Timed auto-lock asks you to unlock again after inactivity; it does not replace a recovery backup.
before: Keep a recoverable backup of your account before changing vault protection.
Have a secure place to store the password you will need to unlock this browser.
checks: The selected timed interval should remain visible in Security after you reopen it.
A vault password is not a recovery phrase or an encrypted backup’s password. Keep those recovery records available independently of this browser.

import.title: Import an existing account
steps: Choose Import Key or Backup during setup, or Add Account → Import Key or Backup from the account selector.
Paste the nsec, hex private key, or recovery phrase privately into the extension, or load your supported backup file.
For an encrypted backup or ncryptsec, enter its backup password. Keep the original backup intact if the format or password is rejected.
Continue after the format is recognized. Set a local vault password when prompted, or unlock an existing vault with its current password.
Finish setup and compare the displayed public key with the identity you intended to restore.
import.overview: Restore an existing identity using its private key, recovery phrase, or supported encrypted backup. The extension detects the input format; an npub alone is a public key and belongs in Watch-Only.
before: Have your existing backup and, if it is encrypted, the password used to encrypt it.
Keep the expected public key and any custom derivation path available to verify the restored identity.
checks: The restored public key should match your saved account. A different key may mean you need the original derivation path.
Importing a phrase starts with its first Nostr key; it does not automatically restore every derived identity or custom path.

switch.title: Switch accounts
steps: Unlock the extension and open the account selector at the top of the popup.
Select the identity you want to use and check its displayed name and public key.
Return to the website. If it still shows the old identity, sign out there and reconnect using the extension.
switch.overview: Switch the active identity before using a different Nostr account. Websites can keep their own signed-in session, so changing the extension’s selection may also require reconnecting there.
before: Add or import each identity you want to switch between.
Check the account name or public key you intend to use.
checks: Check the active account again before approving a new request.
If the website still displays a different profile, verify its own signed-in account rather than assuming the extension selection changed that session.

receive.title: Receive sats
steps: Open Wallet → Deposit.
Enter the amount in sats and create the Lightning invoice.
Share the invoice with the payer. Keep your NWC secret and API key private.
Check wallet activity and balance after the payer sends the payment.
receive.overview: Create a Lightning invoice to receive a chosen amount into your connected wallet. You can share the invoice with the payer without sharing your wallet connection credentials.
before: Connect a wallet and select the account that uses it.
For NWC, ensure the connection permits invoice creation and the information you need to check payment.
checks: Look for a paid invoice or incoming payment in the wallet; creating an invoice alone does not mean it has been paid.
If invoice creation fails, review the wallet connection and its permissions before trying again.

limits.title: Change payment auto-approval
steps: Open Wallet → Settings and find the Auto-Approve Threshold.
Enter a whole number of sats. Use zero if you want each payment to require confirmation.
Save the change, then reopen the settings to check the stored value.
Review wallet activity regularly and lower the threshold or revoke a site’s payment permission if you see unexpected requests.
limits.overview: Automatic approval can let eligible small payments proceed without a confirmation popup. The threshold determines payment eligibility; other permission and safety checks may still require confirmation.
before: Connect the wallet you want to configure and check the active account.
Choose an amount in sats that you are comfortable allowing without reviewing each request.
checks: Payments above the threshold should require confirmation; a payment below it may still require review.
This setting does not give a website permission to use the wallet on its own. Review site access and your wallet provider’s connection permissions separately.

loginFailed.title: I cannot sign in
steps: Open and unlock the extension, then check the active account.
Look for a pending request. Read the requesting site and destination, then approve only if they match the sign-in you started.
Check Permissions → Site rules for a dismissal or relevant denial. Review Backend authentication or Relay authentication when the request involves those destinations.
Return to the website and retry sign-in after resolving the specific problem. If it shows an old account, sign out there before reconnecting.
loginFailed.overview: A sign-in can stop because the vault is locked, the wrong account is selected, or a connection or authentication request is blocked. Start with the pending request and the exact error shown.
before: Open the affected website in the current tab and note any error message.
Identify the account you expect to sign in with.
checks: The website should show the intended account after a successful sign-in.
If the error persists or reports an unsupported request format, keep the exact error and site URL for support. Never include private keys or recovery words.

denied.title: A request is denied
steps: Open Permissions → Site rules for the current website.
If the website is dismissed, review or remove that dismissal so it can ask to connect again.
For an ordinary action, check both site overrides and inherited global rules. Change the relevant denial; a broader Deny may also need attention.
For backend or relay sign-ins, review their separate authentication screens. Retry the action on the website after making the intended change.
denied.overview: A remembered denial can block a request without another approval prompt. The control to change depends on whether the website is dismissed, an ordinary action is denied, or a sign-in destination is blocked.
before: Select the affected account and visit the website making the request.
Note the action or error so you can change the relevant permission.
checks: A removed dismissal allows the website to ask again; it does not automatically connect the site or approve signing.
Resetting site overrides keeps global defaults and separate authentication decisions. Inspect those controls if the request is still denied.

walletFailed.title: My wallet will not connect
steps: In the extension, check whether you selected NWC or LNbits for the credentials you have.
For NWC, paste the complete nostr+walletconnect:// connection secret. Check its expiry and allow wallet information for connection validation.
For LNbits, use the instance’s HTTPS URL and this wallet’s Admin API key. An invoice/read key or administrator password is not a replacement.
Try connecting again, then check which features work. Review balance, invoice, payment, and history permissions in the provider if only some operations fail.
walletFailed.overview: Connection problems often come from a mismatched credential, an expired NWC connection, or an unavailable wallet. Check the connection method before replacing any credentials.
before: Open your wallet provider’s interface and check that the wallet is available.
Keep the connection error visible or copy its text without any secret values.
checks: A successful connection should display the wallet and the information its permissions allow.
If it still fails, provide the connection method and error text to support. Remove NWC secrets and API keys from messages and screenshots.

zapFailed.title: A zap failed
steps: Check wallet activity and the provider’s history before retrying. If the payment is completed, do not send it again just because the app did not update.
If no payment completed, check that the wallet has enough balance for the amount and fees.
Unlock the extension and check the wallet connection, pending requests, and the website’s payment permission.
If the app reports that it cannot find a WebLN provider, refresh the page after unlocking and connecting the wallet.
Retry only after you have established the previous attempt’s outcome. Keep the error text if the request still fails.
zapFailed.overview: A missing success message does not always mean no payment was made. Check the wallet’s actual payment outcome before sending the same zap again.
before: Keep the requested amount and the app’s error message available.
Open the wallet used for the attempted payment.
checks: Use a completed wallet record to confirm payment; the app’s zap display can update separately.
If the outcome remains unknown, keep checking the wallet or contact its provider before paying again. Never share connection secrets when asking for help.

archive.title: Back up and migrate your events
archive.overview: Archive keeps an encrypted local copy of signed events your relays can still return. Download an event file and copy eligible events to another relay. Keep your key backup separately.
before: Unlock the extension and select the account whose events you want to save.
Choose source relays and a safe place for your downloaded event file.
steps: Open Settings → Archive. Use the gear icon to review your source relays, then sync.
Open See details to check each relay result. Retry failed or incomplete sources when needed.
Choose Download archive to save signed events without a file password. Import the file into the matching account to restore events.
Under Migrate archive, choose a destination and review optional event categories. Select Start migration, check eligible events, then Confirm.
checks: Migration copies events without deleting your local archive or data on other relays. The destination may retain its copies.
Uninstalling can remove the local archive. Keep a downloaded copy and back up your keys separately.

connect.title: Connect a remote signer
connect.overview: Use Nostr Connect to keep your private key in a separate signer while browser apps request signatures through Nostr WoT.
before: Install Nostr WoT and a NIP-46-compatible remote signer.
Keep your recovery phrase private; never enter it into the signer connection.
steps: Open the extension and choose Nostr Connect.
Scan the connection QR code with your signer and approve the pairing there.
Review the local connection protection and approve only apps you recognize.
Open a NIP-07 browser app and confirm its signing request appears in your signer.
checks: The signer should complete the request without moving your private key into the browser.
The browser app should receive only the result of the approved signing request.
